bricks.label: struct Queue
bricks.plain_english: Defines the queue — an array, a front index, and a rear index.
bricks.scene_description: An empty horizontal row of boxes appears.

bricks.label: init()
bricks.plain_english: Sets front and rear to -1. The empty queue convention.
bricks.scene_description: FRONT and REAR pointer labels show -1.

bricks.label: enqueue()
bricks.plain_english: Checks for overflow. Increments rear and places value at arr[rear]. Sets front to 0 on the first enqueue.
code_snippet: void enqueue(struct Queue* q, int val) {
bricks.scene_description: New box slides in from the right. REAR arrow moves right.

bricks.label: dequeue()
bricks.plain_english: Checks for underflow. Returns arr[front] and increments front.
bricks.scene_description: Leftmost box slides out. FRONT arrow moves right.

bricks.label: front()
bricks.scene_description: Front box pulses and highlights without moving.

bricks.label: isEmpty()
bricks.plain_english: Returns 1 if front == -1 or front > rear.
bricks.scene_description: FRONT label glows when the queue is empty.

bricks.label: isFull()
bricks.scene_description: Overflow indicator appears at the right end of the row.

bricks.label: display()
bricks.plain_english: Loops from front to rear, printing each element.
code_snippet: for (int i = q->front; i <= q->rear; i++)
bricks.scene_description: Boxes pulse from left to right.
